caption: Supplementary Fig. 27 | Stage-duration associations and the allocation of development time. a, Stage-duration slopes and the direct D-minus-E slope contrast for SST, 200–850-hPa shear, mid-level RH, 200-hPa divergence, 500-hPa ascent and hemisphere-signed 850-hPa vorticity. The common test family contains thirty hypotheses and 2,298 independent SIDs. Effects are 100expβ×reference SD-1, using fixed entry-environment SDs. The D−E contrast exponentiates the difference in log-duration slopes, rather than subtracting percentage responses. Circle area encodes response magnitude and colour its signed value; numbers give the estimates. A dark outline identifies BH q<0.05 and † identifies a primary 95% interval containing zero. The primary intervals use finite-sample SID-cluster covariance with a normal reference; all thirty tests remain in the same Benjamini–Hochberg family. Tables S2a,j report complete estimates, intervals, P/q and counts. b, Environmental coefficients for development fraction DD+E, conditional on exact categorical D+E strata (2,217 SIDs; no additional covariates). Units per environmental increment are °C, m s⁻¹, RH percentage point, 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹, Pa s⁻¹ and 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹, respectively. Points and whiskers show coefficients and primary analytic 95% intervals on separate native-unit axes; P values are shown at right, without an additional BH family. Only 28 of 2,000 auxiliary bootstrap attempts were estimable for the exact-stratum model; these summaries are separate from the displayed analytic inference. Source tables provide all coefficients, reference SDs and interval types. The estimates describe conditional duration associations, without an intervention interpretation.
